questions_and_answers.question_text: With which word do all the verbs discussed so far form the negative?
Which verb is the single exception?
What is the irregular negative form of yǒu?
Write the Chinese for "He doesn't have any American friends."
Give the two possible English translations of Tā yǒu Yīngguo péngyou.
What does the verb yǒu mean?
Would it be correct to say bù yǒu?

answers.answer_text: No — yǒu is irregular and forms its negative as méiyou, not with bù.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese question meaning "Does Mr. Liú have any American friends?"

answers.answer_text: Liú Xiānsheng yǒu Měiguo péngyou ma?

questions_and_answers.question_text: Why can Tā yǒu Yīngguo péngyou be translated two ways?

answers.answer_text: Because Chinese nouns have the same form for singular and plural, so péngyou may be "friend" or "friends."

questions_and_answers.question_text: Which is the only verb so far with an irregular negative?

articles.text:
2. B: Liú Xiānsheng yǒu Měiguo             Does Mr. Liú have any American
      péngyou ma?                           friends?
   A: Tā méiyou Měiguo péngyou.             He doesn't have any American
                                            friends.
   A: Tā yǒu Yīngguo péngyou.               He has English friends. OR
                                            He has an English friend.

Note on No. 2

Méiyou: All the verbs discussed so far form the negative with bù, with the single exception of yǒu, "to have," which has the irregular negative form méiyou.
